title: OpenStax publisher lexicon (Layer 3)
description: Publisher-specific marker strings -> Layer-2 instructional-profile roles for OpenStax-shaped open textbooks. Layer 3 of the universal block-label ontology: this is the ONLY layer where publisher-specific marker vocabulary is allowed to live (wide-net rule: publisher vocabulary is DATA, never code). Matching is case-insensitive PREFIX on the block's leading text.
$comment: Marker set lifted from align_gold.py PRACTICE_MARKER_LEXICON['openstax'] + the SemantiK open-textbook overlay (schemas/taxonomies/semantik_lexicon.json). 'try it is something that only really appears in openstax texts' (owner 2026-07-13) — so it is confined here, not in the generic lexicon. Roles reference genre_profile_instructional.json.

x-markers.notes: immediate-practice prompt after a worked example; e.g. 'TRY IT :: 1.173'

x-frontmatter.$comment: Publisher-specific colophon + marketing marker strings for the front-matter / donor / marketing chunk classifier (Trainforge/chunker/frontmatter.py). Wide-net rule: publisher vocabulary is DATA, never code. The GENERIC copyright tokens (creative commons, ISBN, all rights reserved, copyright, ©, trademark) and the hard math-content veto stay in code; only these publisher-named phrases live here. Matching is case-insensitive substring with internal-whitespace tolerance. Loaded via lib.ontology.taxonomy.load_taxonomy with a frozen code fallback (mirrors the region_map lexicon pattern).

x-eoc-banners.$comment: Publisher-specific end-of-chapter (EOC) exercise/drill banner names for the SemanticStructureExtractor noncontent-heading filter (lib/semantic_structure_extractor/semantic_structure_extractor.py). Generic academic apparatus wording ('review exercises','section exercises','additional practice','writing exercises') stays in code; only these publisher-named banners live here. 'exact' = whole-heading (normalized) match; 'prefix' = heading-opening match ('<phrase><separator>...section topic'). Loaded via load_taxonomy with a frozen code fallback.
